enforcement_note: The hook writes behavioural metrics but verifies nothing about application-level audit logging.
condition: When actions need to be reconstructable after the fact.
rule: Audit what is logged, retained and attributable, as questions.
ai_action: Work through the checklist against the code in question. Report the answers, including the ones that pass -- a checklist that only ever surfaces problems reads as noise. Where an answer is 'I cannot tell from here', say so rather than assuming the safe answer.

checklist.question: Are authentication attempts logged, successful and failed alike?
checklist.remediation_hint: Log both outcomes with the metadata needed to investigate.

checklist.question: Can an action be attributed to an actor without guessing?
checklist.remediation_hint: Record the subject identifier alongside the action.

checklist.question: Would the log survive the incident it records, or can the same actor erase it?
Is anything logged that would be a breach if the log leaked?
checklist.remediation_hint: Redact at the boundary; log identifiers, not payloads.
checklist.revalidation_note: OWASP Top 10:2025 is in release candidate. Re-check this item against the final release; a release candidate is not yet citable as authoritative.
checklist.group_condition: When logs carry personal or sensitive data

checklist.question: Is there a stated retention period, or do logs accumulate indefinitely?
checklist.remediation_hint: Set and enforce a retention window.
checklist.group_condition: When logs carry personal or sensitive data

anti_pattern: Do not convert these questions into prescriptions. A question makes you look at the code and survives a codebase it was not written for; a prescription tells you what to type and stops being right the moment the context differs.

provenance.source: agent-generated; every item cites a source resolved on 2026-08-05
provenance.basis: Adopted from docs/checklist-system.md (Professional Hierarchical Checklist System + Golden Rule Research Protocol). Items phrased as review questions per the checklist-not-prescription rule.

risk_weight_note: The accountability band (8-10) assumes a fleet with diffused ownership. On a single-operator repository a gap in the audit trail is recoverable from git history, so the honest weight sits below the imported band.
